sec.name: Security
sec.short: Threats, attack surface, supply chain, vulnerability response.
sec.what: Looks at threats: attack surface, secure defaults, supply chain and how vulnerabilities are handled.
asks: What could an attacker do here?
What data or capability would be exposed?
What are the supply-chain risks of each option?
What security obligations apply?

acts.discover: Applicable in DISCOVER: considered when scanning options (1.4) and assessing risk (1.5) — before any commitment.

priv.name: Privacy
priv.short: Data minimisation, lawful basis, consent, subject rights.
priv.what: Looks at personal data: minimisation, lawful basis, consent, subject rights and privacy by design.
asks: What personal data is involved?
What's the lawful basis and consent?
Can we use less?
How long is it kept?
decisions: Is the personal-data use lawful and proportionate?

acts.discover: Required when observing users (1.3.2) and applicable to stakeholder maps, experiments and research data throughout.

infra.name: Infrastructure / Platform
infra.what: Looks at environments and platforms: capacity, hosting, platform services and infrastructure as code.
asks: What platform would it run on?
Is new infrastructure needed?
What does it cost to host?

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER; relevant if feasibility depends on platform changes.

perf.name: Performance
perf.short: Latency, throughput, scalability under real load.
perf.what: Looks at speed and scale: latency, throughput and efficiency under realistic load.
asks: How many users / transactions?
How fast must it respond?
What happens at peak?
ignored: Systems that collapse under real use

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER; relevant if volumes affect feasibility.

vendor.name: Vendor / Third Party
vendor.short: Dependency risk, SLAs, lock-in, exit strategy.
vendor.what: Looks at third parties: dependency risk, service levels, lock-in, due diligence and exit.
asks: Which third parties would we depend on?
How healthy and secure are they?
What happens if they fail or change terms?
How would we exit?
ignored: Stranded on a failing or expensive vendor

acts.discover: Applicable when buy / partner options appear (1.4.2) and when vendor commitment is needed.

ops.name: Operations
ops.what: Looks at running the thing: operability, monitoring, support processes and the day-two cost of every decision.
asks: Who will run and support it?
What does it cost to operate?
How will problems be detected?

acts.discover: Applicable during feasibility and risk (1.5) to surface run cost and operability.

qa.name: Quality / Testing
qa.short: Fitness for purpose, defect prevention, test strategy.
qa.what: Looks at fitness for purpose and confidence: how we'll know it works, and how defects will be prevented rather than found late.
asks: How will we know it works?
What would 'good enough' look like?
What are the riskiest areas to test?

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER; becomes required from BUILD.

arch.name: Architecture
arch.what: Looks at structure and quality attributes: how the solution fits the existing landscape and which decisions will be expensive to reverse.
asks: How does this fit our current systems?
Which quality attributes matter most?
Which decisions are hard to reverse?
What integration and data impacts are there?
decisions: Does the approach fit the architecture?

acts.discover: Applicable in DISCOVER: maps the current state (1.1), weighs solution options (1.4) and reviews feasibility (1.5).

eng.name: Engineering
eng.what: Looks at implementability: can it be built and maintained with our technology, skills and time, at sustainable quality?
asks: Can we build this with what we have?
What are the technical unknowns?
What will it cost to maintain?
What skills are missing?

acts.discover: Required for the feasibility decision (1.5); applicable when scanning solutions and technology (1.4).

data.name: Data
data.what: Looks at data: what's available, its quality and lineage, what new data is needed and how it is kept, migrated and used.
asks: What data exists, and is it trustworthy?
What new data will we need?
How will we measure outcomes?
Who owns the data?

acts.discover: Applicable for usage analysis in research (1.3), experiment metrics (1.4) and sizing (1.4.4).

req.name: Requirements
req.short: Clear, testable, traceable needs; controlled change.
req.what: Looks at needs as requirements: clear, testable, traceable statements, with conflicts and changes controlled.
asks: Is each need stated clearly and testably?
Where does each requirement come from?
Do any requirements conflict?
How will changes be controlled?
decisions: Is the requirements baseline good enough to plan from?
ignored: Rework and disputes over what was meant

acts.discover: Applicable in DISCOVER: validated problems and JTBD become the stakeholder needs that PLAN turns into requirements.

rel.name: Reliability / Resilience
rel.what: Looks at availability and resilience: failure tolerance, recovery and graceful degradation.
asks: How available must it be?
What happens when parts fail?
How fast must it recover?

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER; becomes required in DESIGN and OPERATE.

ai.name: AI / ML
ai.short: Model fitness, evaluation, drift, bias, oversight.
ai.what: Looks at the use of AI and machine learning: whether a model is fit for purpose, how it's evaluated, and how bias, drift and human oversight are handled.
asks: Is AI actually needed here?
How will we evaluate model quality?
What happens when it's wrong?
Where is human oversight?

acts.discover: Applicable when AI is part of an option (1.4) — and when AI assistants are used to synthesise research, their output is checked by people.

legal.name: Legal
legal.what: Looks at contracts, licensing, intellectual property, liability, terms and jurisdiction.
asks: What contracts or licences are involved?
Who owns the IP?
What liability could arise?
Which jurisdictions apply?

acts.discover: Applicable for sensitive ideas (1.2.1), competitive intelligence and IP (1.4) and public experiments (1.4.3).

cust.name: Customer / User
cust.short: Real users, their jobs, and what adoption requires.
cust.what: Looks at the work from the point of view of the people who will use it or be affected by it: their jobs, pains, contexts and what adoption would really take.
asks: Who exactly are the users, and in which situations?
What job are they trying to get done?
What do they do today instead?
What would make them switch — or refuse?
decisions: Is the problem real for users?

items: When…, I want…, so I can…

ignored: Solving a problem users don't have

acts.discover: Required in DISCOVER: users are researched in 1.3, demand is proven with behaviour in 1.4, and user value is scored in 1.5.

a11y.name: Accessibility
a11y.short: Usable by people with disabilities; WCAG.
a11y.what: Looks at access for people with disabilities: conformance with WCAG and support for assistive technologies.
asks: Can people with disabilities use it?
Did research include them?
Which accessibility standard applies?

cells: Does it work with assistive tech?

acts.discover: Applicable in research planning and observation (1.3) — recruit for diversity of ability.

prod.name: Product
prod.short: Problem–solution fit, scope, prioritisation, outcomes over output.
prod.what: Looks at the work as a product: is there a real problem, for real users, solved in a way that's coherent with the rest of the product and measured by outcomes rather than output?
asks: What problem are we solving, for whom?
What outcome will change, and how will we measure it?
Is the scope the smallest that proves value?
How does this fit the product's direction?
decisions: What's in and out of scope?

items: In user terms, no solution words

ignored: No way to tell if it worked

acts.discover: Required in DISCOVER: product owns framing (1.2), the validated problem (1.3), demand evidence (1.4) and the decision recommendation (1.5).

biz.name: Business / Strategy
biz.short: Strategic fit, value hypothesis, opportunity cost.
biz.what: Looks at the work through the organisation's strategy: does this move a goal that matters, is it worth more than the alternatives we're giving up, and does it fit how the business creates value?
asks: Which strategic goal or OKR does this move?
What's the value hypothesis — and how will we know?
What are we not doing if we do this (opportunity cost)?
Why now?
concerns: Pet projects with no strategic link
decisions: Is it worth more than the next-best use of the money?
ignored: Teams build things nobody senior will fund or adopt
Initiatives survive on momentum, not value

acts.discover: Required throughout DISCOVER: it frames the opportunity against strategy (1.1), keeps framing honest about value (1.2), sizes the prize (1.4) and drives the Go / Kill decision (1.5).

fin.name: Finance / Commercial
fin.short: Cost, funding, pricing, unit economics, return.
fin.what: Looks at money: cost, funding, pricing, unit economics and the return the initiative must justify.
asks: What will it cost — to build and to run?
What is the return, and over what period?
How is it funded, and is that within limits?
What does a unit of value cost and earn?
decisions: Is it within the sponsor's investment limit?
ignored: Approved initiatives that can't be afforded to run

acts.discover: Required for sizing (1.4) and the decision (1.5); applicable when scoping discovery spend (1.2).

ux.name: UX / CX
ux.short: Usability, journeys and the end-to-end experience.
ux.what: Looks at the end-to-end experience: usability, journeys, content and every touchpoint — not just screens.
asks: What does the whole journey look like, across channels?
Where do people struggle, wait or drop off?
Can they understand and use it without help?
Is the experience consistent?
concerns: Screen-level thinking that misses the journey

acts.discover: Required in 1.3 (observing real journeys) and applicable when framing ideas and validating demand.

sup.name: Support / Service Mgmt
sup.short: Service readiness and the customer's path to help.
sup.what: Looks at service readiness: support models, knowledge and the customer's path to help.
asks: Who will customers contact?
What will support need to know?
What new requests will arrive?

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER — but support teams are a rich source of problem evidence in 1.3 and 1.4.

dom.name: Domain / Business Process
dom.short: Business rules, process flows, vocabulary, invariants.
dom.what: Looks at the business domain itself: the processes, rules, vocabulary and invariants the software must respect.
asks: What are the real business processes and rules here?
What words does the business use, and what do they mean?
Which rules can never be broken?
Where do processes cross teams or systems?
decisions: Which business rules constrain the solution?
ignored: Rework late in BUILD when rules surface
Data and process errors in production

acts.discover: Required in DISCOVER: it maps the current state and constraints (1.1) and grounds the real problem in actual workflows (1.3).

comp.name: Compliance / Regulatory
comp.short: Obligations and the evidence that proves them.
comp.what: Looks at obligations from regulators and certifications, and the evidence needed to show they're met.
asks: Which regulations or certifications apply?
What do they require of this solution?
What evidence will auditors expect?
Are there hard blockers?

acts.discover: Required when scanning constraints (1.1.4); applicable in risk assessment (1.5).

gov.name: Governance / Risk
gov.short: Decision rights, risk appetite, auditable controls.
gov.what: Looks at decision rights, risk appetite and controls: who may decide what, and whether there's an auditable trail from decision to evidence.
asks: Who has authority to decide?
Is the risk within appetite?
Is the decision recorded with its evidence?
What must be escalated?

acts.discover: Required at the sponsor step (1.1.1), stakeholder decision rights (1.1.3), risk (1.5.3) and the decision (1.5.4).

devops.name: DevOps / Delivery
devops.what: Looks at the delivery pipeline: flow, automation and deployment safety.
asks: Can we deliver this incrementally?
What pipeline changes are needed?

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER; required from BUILD.

i18n.name: Localization / i18n
i18n.what: Looks at reach across languages and regions: locales, formats, regional rules and culturally appropriate content.
asks: Which regions and languages?
Do rules or formats differ by region?

acts.discover: Rarely engaged in DISCOVER unless the opportunity is multi-region.
